---
title: Installation
description: Install polars-umap from PyPI and check that it works.
---

polars-umap is a single package on PyPI. Its only dependency is Polars.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## uv

```bash
uv add polars-umap
```

## pip

```bash
pip install polars-umap
```

:::

## Requirements

- **Python** 3.9 or newer.
- **Polars** 1.0 or newer, including Polars 2.x.

Wheels are available for Linux (x86-64 and ARM64, glibc and musl), macOS (Intel and Apple
Silicon) and Windows (x86-64). They use the stable Python ABI, so one wheel works for every Python
version from 3.9 on.

## Check the installation

```python
import polars as pl
import polars_umap as pu

print(pu.__version__)

df = pl.DataFrame({"x": range(100), "y": [i % 7 for i in range(100)]})
df.umap.fit_transform("x", "y", random_state=0)
```

If this prints a version number and returns a frame with `umap_0` and `umap_1` columns, you're
all set.

::: {.callout-note}
## Import to register the namespace

The `.umap` namespace on expressions and frames only exists after `import polars_umap`. If you
get `AttributeError: 'Expr' object has no attribute 'umap'`, you've forgotten that import.
:::

## GPU support

The wheels include GPU support through [wgpu](https://wgpu.rs). It uses Metal on macOS and Vulkan
or DirectX 12 elsewhere, and needs no extra installation. Pass `gpu=True` to use it; see
[Performance](performance.qmd) for when that helps.

## Building from source

If there's no wheel for your platform, pip builds polars-umap from the source distribution. That
needs:

- a [Rust toolchain](https://rustup.rs) (stable), and
- network access, because the UMAP implementation is fetched from the
  [embedding-atlas](https://github.com/apple/embedding-atlas) repository at a pinned commit.

To work on polars-umap itself:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/jeroenjanssens/polars-umap
cd polars-umap
uv sync                                             # builds the extension
uv run maturin develop --uv --profile dev-release  # faster rebuilds while developing
uv run pytest -n auto
```
